Non-technical users who don't use Linux (Gnu/Linux) may have trouble installing programs and especially compilers. Some IDEs come bundled with compilers while some compilers are a complete joke to install... for non technical or lazy users of course (everyone).

There needs to be an IDE that works in the browser and uses your machine's hardware directly. You would visit the site or add an extension or even download the browser app, select the compiler you need for your language, and it installs one for you so you can also work offline from that machine. This IDE should also serve as a text editor if a compiler wasn't installed, meaning it supports syntax highlighting and what not.

http://coliru.stacked-crooked.com/

http://cpp.sh/

The above almost-solutions have short (~5s) run-time limits and you must be online to run your code.

On another note, the great [Code::Blocks](http://www.codeblocks.org/) IDE whose download is unfortunately hosted on sourceforge, bundles C/C++/Fortran compilers and lets you choose which to install. And it installs them successfully without putting you through the GCC to windows compatibility bull shit. Another request of mine would be to have someone extract this compiler installer from Code::Blocks (GPLv3) and maintain an executable for Windows and possibly other systems.

It's that bad.

**edit** Why in the browser? Everyone will have one, there should be nothing extra to install, just share the website name.
